newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian lev funds demand edges up, rates fall.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian lev funds demand edges up, rates fall.

text.p: Demand for Bulgarian interbank deposits edged up on Wednesday due to treasury paper payments, but supply was very high and lev funds rates fell, dealers said.
"Banks bid for short-term deposits in order to pay for the government securities they bought on Monday," said a dealer.
On Monday, financial institutions bought two discount T-bill issues with three- and 12-month maturities with a total par of 80 billion levs ($45.7 million).
Overnight interbank depo rates eased to 4.0-4.5 percent annual from 4.5-5.0 percent on Tuesday.
Spot week rates were unchanged at 6.0-6.5 percent annually, but this was due to the lack of demand for such periods, traders said.
The central bank cut its simple annual main interest rate to 9.76 percent from 10.12 percent, in effect since Monday.
-- Dessislava Popova, Sofia Newsroom +359-2 981 4145 ($ = 1751 Bulgarian Levs)
